newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG SEEK REHABILITATION AGAINST AEK ATHENS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG SEEK REHABILITATION AGAINST AEK ATHENS.

text.p: French glamour club Paris St Germain, their morale in tatters, will be looking for a face-saving victory over AEK Athens in their European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final first leg on Thursday.
The holders, aiming for a fifth successive European semifinal, sank to a new low on Saturday with elimination from the French Cup by fourth division amateurs.
A good Cup Winners' Cup performance has already seen PSG through one crisis this season when they beat Galatasaray 4-0 at home in October to reach the quarter-finals 6-4 on aggregate.
PSG manager Ricardo expressed his concern when he said: "From what I've seen in Athens, and after our match at Clermont, I'm not (feeling) very reassured."
Their Greek opponents on Thursday will surely not, however, be as generous as the Turks, while PSG were not suffering then from a total collapse in team morale.
AEK coach Petros Ravousis, whose side have been cast in the role of favourites by the French media, said: "We are going to Paris to do the best we can.
"PSG are the holders and the favourites. But we are in good form and not facing any injuries." AEK will be without suspended midfielder Christos Maladenis.
At the back the Greeks rely strongly on the experience of their veteran 1994 World Cup stopper Stelios Manolas.
Striker Demis Nikolaidis, top scorer in Greek league, could give the runaround to a PSG defence seriously short of confidence.
Working behind closed doors with his players since Tuesday, Ricardo is pondering team changes with a squad depleted by injury to three defenders.
"I have a choice between experienced players who are low psychologically and youngsters whose morale has been affected less," he said.
France international Vicent Guerin is so off his game he is almost certain to start on the bench with Jerome Leroy taking his place in midfield.

But with Alain Roche, Jimmy Algerino and Didier Domi all injured, Ricardo will not be able to also drop veteran Paul Le Guen, who like Guerin played badly on Saturday before they both had their penalties saved in the decisive shoot-out.
Fabrice Kelban is a reserve central defender with very limited first division experience and Ricardo may not want to risk plunging him in at the deep end.

The key may be the performance of Brazil's Leonardo, who inspired the fightback against Galatasaray. But even he, who missed the Clermont debacle, could not produce the goods in a very poor 1-1 home draw against Guingamp 11 days ago.
Brazilian captain Rai believes the competition alone ought to generate enough motivation.
"In European cups the motivation comes on its own. It's particular to all the big European clubs," he said.
Probable teams:
Paris St Germain - Bernard Lama; Laurent Fournier, Bruno N'Gotty, Paul Le Guen, Daniel Kenedy; Jerome Leroy, Benoit Cauet, Rai, Leonardo; Patrice Loko, Cyrille Pouget.

AEK Athens - Ilias Atmatsidis; Michalis Kasapis, Stelios Manolas, Nikos Kostenoglou, Vaios Karayannis, Tony Savevski, Timour Ketspayia, Christos Costis, Daniel Batista, Demis Nikolaidis, Vassilis Borbokis.
